title: Churn Risk Scorecard and Rapid Response Playbook
content:
TL;DR: Working playbook + scorecard to quickly triage renewal risk, run automated saves for low-medium risk, and trigger a time-boxed exec escalation for high-risk, high-ARR customers. Built for Redwood-specific failure modes (throughput/latency regressions, Dedicated capacity incidents, private deployment security concerns, model quality regressions).
Purpose: Provide a reproducible, measurable path from signal -> diagnosis -> mitigation -> exec escalation. Meant to be used in weekly QBR prep and real-time renewal risk scrubs.
Scope: Customers with active renewals within 12 months. Special handling rules for Dedicated/Private deals (see "Technical remediation" below).
Definitions (quick):
- Risk Score (0-100): Composite numeric used to prioritize outreach. Higher = higher probability of churn.
- ARR at Risk: Annualized revenue tied to renewal window.
- Tier classifications: Tier A (> $250k ARR), Tier B ($50k–$250k), Tier C (< $50k).
Scorecard (working rubric) — combine automated signals + qualitative inputs. We recommend automating base signal collection then adding CS annotated points.
- Signals (weighted):
  - Usage delta (last 30d vs prior 30d): 25 points (drop >50% = full 25)
  - Support volume & severity (P0/P1 incidents in last 90d): 20 points
  - Latency SLO breaches or error-rate spikes (hosted/dedicated/private): 15 points
  - Feature adoption (routes used vs contracted): 10 points
  - Billing anomalies / overages (surprise charges, disputed invoices): 10 points
  - Exec sponsor engagement (no meetings in 90d): 10 points (lack of engagement adds risk)
  - Open escalations unresolved >10d: 5 points
  - Product quality regressions (model hallucination / throughput regression flagged by evals): 5 points
Scoring example (quick):
- Customer X: Usage drop 60% (25), P1 incident 1x (10), latency breach last week (15), exec unreachable (10) => 60/100 => Medium-High risk.
Signal thresholds -> actions (playbook tiers):
- Low (0–24): Automated touches and nurture
  - Automated email sequence (see template A)
  - Run basic health check (billing, API keys, quota)
  - Owner: CSM-queue (rotating)
  - Timeline: 2 weeks
- Medium (25–59): Proactive CS + technical runbook
  - CSM weekly cadence + technical deep-dive call
  - Open a cross-functional investigation ticket (tag: CS-MED-RISK)
  - Recommended mitigations: prefix caching review, endpoint routing audit, model variant fallback enablement
  - Owner: Assigned CSM + Solutions Engineer
  - Timeline: 2–6 weeks depending on root cause
- High (60–100): Rapid response + exec escalation
  - 24–48h rapid-response war room (CS lead, Solutions Eng, SRE, Product Owner)
  - Customer exec briefing within 72h
  - Formal exec escalation if unresolved at 7 days for Tier A
  - Possible offers: targeted credits, custom model tuning, Dedicated capacity swap, SLA concession
Runbook steps (detailed) — Medium/High only (checklist style):
1) Immediate triage (owner: on-call CSM)
   - Pull dashboard: token consumption, route-level latency, error-rate, recent deploys (last 14 days)
   - Lookup recent support tickets and engineering PRs that touched serving-runtime
   - Confirm whether customer is on Hosted / Dedicated / Private (affects remediation options)
2) Technical diagnosis (owner: SE + on-call SRE)
   - Verify model variant routing and available fallbacks
   - Check KV cache warmup stats and continuous batching behavior
   - Look at GPU saturation for Dedicated pools; check autoscale events
   - For Private: confirm network/KMS logs for recent config changes
3) Mitigation actions (pick applicable):
   - Roll back recent model or infra deploy if correlated to incident
   - Enable model variant fallback to a compatible lower-latency model; notify customer
   - Short-term token quota increases or credits to prevent functional loss
   - Apply batching tuning or limit max concurrency for problematic routes
   - Provide a tailored evaluation run (sample prompts) to validate quality after change
4) Communication (owner: CSM)
   - 24h update note to customer + internal Slack warroom
   - Share remediation ETA and next steps
   - Book exec check-in if Tier A or unresolved after 3 days
Templates (quick, copy-paste):
- Email subject (rapid): "Immediate: remediation plan and next steps for {{customer_name}}"
- Email body (short): "Hi {{sponsor_first}}, we’ve opened a rapid-response for the issue you reported. Initial diagnosis shows [summary]. Actions we are taking: 1) [action], 2) [action]. We’ll update in 24h and have a call scheduled for {{call_time}}. — {{csm_name}}"
- Exec briefing slide bullets (for QBR): Problem summary, impact (tokens/requests lost, latency delta, impacted business flows), actions taken, ask from customer (SLA/credits/POC), next milestones.
Renewal tracker columns (sheet spec, simple):
  - customer_id, customer_name, ARR, renewal_date, CSM_owner, last_meeting_date, risk_score, tier, primary_signal, last_action, next_touch_date, open_escalation (Y/N), notes
Operational notes and automation TODOs (working):
- TODO: Wire automated Risk Score into CS dashboard (source: usage API + billing + support) — ticket JIRA-CS-507
- TODO: Add a one-click "open war room" slack action to create channel and triage checklist
- TODO: Add model-quality eval output to signals (Evals pipeline link) — depends on research team
Escalation matrix (who to call):
- Tier A, >$250k, severity P1 unresolved >24h: CSM + Head of CS + VP Eng + SRE on-call + Solutions Eng
- Tier B, P1 unresolved >72h: CSM + Director CS + SE on-call
- All: Legal/compliance loop-in for contract disputes or security incidents (Private deployments)
Special handling: Dedicated & Private
- Dedicated: If GPU pool saturation or autoscale fail -> offer put-through capacity swap. Consider temporary credits if performance failure caused business impact.
- Private: Engage assigned deployment engineer and security lead immediately. Network changes or KMS events often require customer coordination for remediation windows.
Save plays (catalog: quick list with execution notes):
- Usage ramp play: 2-week pilot for new high-value routes + customer success workshop on integration best practices
- Technical POC: Free SE hours (x10) to tune batching/quantization for top 3 routes
- Business concession: one-time credit equivalent to X% of AR to maintain relationship while fix is in-flight
- Contract structuring: short-term renewal + ramp clause; move to Dedicated reserved capacity with price protections
Measurement & success metrics:
- Time to first contact (goal <24h for high risk)
- Time to remediation or accepted workaround (goal <7d for Tier A)
- Renewal outcome: closed-won retained / churned / downsized
- Post-mortem: loss prevented? NRR impact measured at 30/90/180d
QBR prep checklist (CSM to fill prior to exec QBR):
- Risk score history (last 90d)
- Actions taken and current status
- Exec outreach notes + date of last sponsor contact
- Concrete asks required from the customer or internal teams
Retro template (after action):
- What happened (timeline)
- Root cause
- What we did well
- What failed (process/tooling gaps)
- Action items (owner + due date)
Open questions / decisions required (notes to self):
- Should score weighting change for tier A customers? (currently same algorithm) — need product input
- How to encode model-quality signals from evals into a time-series? (SEs want per-route rollup)
- What standard concessions are pre-approved for Tier A vs Tier B? (legal to confirm)
Appendix: Example play for a Dedicated customer with AI latency regressions
1) Verify autoscale & pool health -> increase reserved capacity as temporary mitigation
2) Route traffic to alternative region/model variant if latency SLO breached
3) Provide customer with daily service report until SLA is stable
4) Propose a dedicated performance review and optimizations workshop (SE priced item)
Notes to reviewers: This doc is intentionally informal. Aim is to iterate quickly and bake into the CS console. Please add comments inline or drop suggestions to #cs-renewal-playbooks.

[END]
